changeSet.author: nexus-hzhgl
changeSet.comment:
nexus-hzhgl (RDR-191 Phase 3/4 pre-flight, conexus relay [22411] ASK B): grant the built-in pg_monitor role to nexus_svc so the engine can read pg_ls_waldir() and the pg_stat_* monitoring views/functions -- WAL-retention visibility during the Phase 4 always-copy trough window (trough = 11,360 MiB - X; breaches the 10,000 MiB floor if retained WAL X exceeds ~1,360 MiB). Before this grant pg_ls_waldir() is permission-denied to nexus_svc, so retained WAL was entirely unobservable.
CAVEAT (conexus relay [22411], correcting an earlier assumption): pg_monitor does NOT provide filesystem free space. It is WAL-retention visibility ONLY -- the disk-free-space gate is a separate ask, conexus's own Crunchy Bridge API key path. Neither substitutes for the other.
WHY THIS SUCCEEDS UNDER A NOSUPERUSER MIGRATION ROLE: granting membership in a role requires the grantor to already hold that role WITH ADMIN OPTION (or be superuser) -- nexus_admin (NOCREATEROLE, NOSUPERUSER) cannot self-provision that the way it can an ordinary schema-owned GRANT. The bootstrap superuser must first run `GRANT pg_monitor TO nexus_admin WITH ADMIN OPTION`, exactly the same shape as nexus_diag's BYPASSRLS in grants-nexus-diag.xml -- an attribute/ privilege only a superuser can confer, so it lives OUTSIDE this changelog: src/nexus/db/pg_provision.py for the local bundle (_create_roles for a from-scratch provision, _backfill_pg_monitor_admin_option from provision()'s fast idempotency path for an EXISTING install -- round 2, code-review-expert Critical 2026-08-13: _create_roles alone is unreached on every already- provisioned local install, the steady state for upgrades), and docs/configuration.md's bring-your-own-Postgres DBA prerequisites for managed deployments.
TRADEOFF, recorded deliberately (substantive-critic round 2, T2 [22418]): WITH ADMIN OPTION lets nexus_admin grant or revoke pg_monitor membership to ANY role, not just nexus_svc -- a small widening of nexus_admin's role-grant blast radius. Accepted because the changelog (running as nexus_admin) is exactly where such grants are supposed to originate as the durable record; the narrower alternative (superuser grants pg_monitor to nexus_svc directly) would bypass the changelog and drift on any credential-domain rebuild.
FAIL-LOUD WITH A NAMED REMEDY, NEVER A SILENT SKIP (round 2, code-review-expert Important 2026-08-13): unlike grants-nexus-diag-1's clean skip-when-absent (an OPTIONAL diagnostic role), nexus_svc's WAL-retention visibility is not optional once shipped, and nothing in code enforces that a bring-your-own/managed deployment's DBA has run the ADMIN OPTION prerequisite before this changeset executes -- especially on the FIRST boot after upgrading to an engine that carries this changeset. Rather than let that surface as a bare "permission denied to grant role pg_monitor" (which names no remedy), the inner GRANT is wrapped to catch exactly that failure and re-raise a self-explanatory error naming the fix -- the same "loud, not silent" posture as grants-nexus-svc-1's REQUIRED-nexus_svc fail-fast, applied to a permission gap instead of a missing role. No MARK_RAN degrade, no preConditions skip: a reproducible, WAL-visibility-is-a-probe absence must never masquerade as a vacuous pass.
IDEMPOTENCY: GRANT of role membership is naturally idempotent in PostgreSQL (re-granting an already-held membership is a no-op); runAlways="true" self-heals a nexus_svc created after the first migration run, same as every other changeset in this file.
pg_monitor is a built-in PostgreSQL role (PG10+) -- no version guard needed, unlike the PG17+-only MAINTAIN privilege above.
